translation: Pallavi (Chorus): I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal), I'll bring you blouses of every colour (I'll bring you blouses of every colour) (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal, I'll bring you blouses of every colour). Put on the bangles, girl, so all your longings are fulfilled (Put on the bangles, girl, so all your longings are fulfilled). Manjula... I've set my heart on you, my cousin... am I not your own cousin, your bava? (Manjula, I've set my heart on you, O my cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?) (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal, I'll bring you blouses of every colour)

Verse 1: When you come along in your hook-fastened blouse, your bosom full and ripe (When you come along in your hook-fastened blouse, your bosom full and ripe), O slender-waisted girl, I can't live without you, my love (O slender-waisted girl, I can't live without you, my love). Curling ringlets of hair, braids with golden tassels (Curling ringlets of hair, braids with golden tassels). Manjula... I've set my heart on you, my cousin... am I not your own cousin, your bava? (Manjula, I've set my heart on you, O my cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?) (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal, I'll bring you blouses of every colour)

Verse 2: Girl with toe-rings that jingle jal-jal, girl with long sliding braids (Girl with toe-rings that jingle jal-jal, girl with long sliding braids). A flash of lightning between your cheeks, and rain pours down in my heart (A flash of lightning between your cheeks, and rain pours down in my heart). For the beauty spot on your cheek, I've given you my heart (For the beauty spot on your cheek, I've given you my heart). Manjula... I've set my heart on you, my cousin... am I not your own cousin, your bava? (Manjula, I've set my heart on you, O my cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?) (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal, I'll bring you blouses of every colour)

Verse 3: I'll load your hands with jewellery, I'll build you a famous bungalow (I'll load your hands with jewellery, I'll build you a famous bungalow). I'll take your hand, I'll tie the tali around your neck (I'll take your hand, I'll tie the tali around your neck). I'll marry you so you never know hardship (I'll marry you so you never know hardship). Manjula... I've set my heart on you, my cousin... am I not your own cousin, your bava? (Manjula, I've set my heart on you, O my cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?) (I'll bring you bangles that jingle gal-gal, I'll bring you blouses of every colour) (Put on the bangles, girl, so all your longings are fulfilled) (Manjula, I've set my heart on you... my cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?...) (My cousin, am I not your own cousin, your bava?...)
summaryEn:
A love song sung by a young man to Manjula, his maradalu (cousin). He reminds her that he is her menabava, her own cross-cousin. Marriage between such cousins has long been an accepted, even favoured, match in many Telugu families, and the singer uses that bond as his claim on her. He tempts her with gifts: bangles that jingle 'gal gal', blouses in every colour, a handful of jewellery and a grand bungalow. He praises her hook-fastened blouse, slender waist, curling hair, braids with golden tassels, jingling toe-rings and the beauty spot on her cheek. The song ends with a promise to take her hand, tie the tali (the marriage pendant) and keep her free from hardship.

In form, the song is a call-and-response: nearly every phrase is sung and then echoed, probably by a chorus. Sound words such as 'gal gal' for bangles and 'jal jal' for toe-rings add to the rhythm, and the image of lightning on her cheeks bringing rain to his heart gives it a lyrical touch. The long refrain 'Manjula... am I not your own bava?' closes every verse.

మరదలు మంజులను ఉద్దేశించి ఒక యువకుడు పాడే ప్రేమ పాట ఇది. ‘నేను నీ మేనబావను కాదా’ అని ఆమెకు గుర్తుచేస్తూ, మేనరికం సంబంధాన్నే తన హక్కుగా చూపిస్తాడు. తెలుగు కుటుంబాల్లో మేనబావ–మరదలు పెళ్లి చాలాకాలంగా ఆమోదం పొందిన, ఇష్టపడే సంబంధం. ‘గల్ గల్’ మోగే గాజులు, రంగు రంగుల రైకలు, చేతి నిండా నగలు, పేరున్న బంగ్లా ఇస్తానని ఆశపెడతాడు. కుండీల రైక, సన్నని నడుము, ఉంగరాల కురులు, బంగారు కుచ్చుల జడలు, ‘జల్ జల్’ మోగే మట్టెలు, బుగ్గ మీద మచ్చ అంటూ ఆమె అందాన్ని పొగుడుతాడు. చివర్లో వేలు పట్టి, మెడలో తాళి కట్టి, కష్టాలు లేకుండా చూసుకుంటానని మాట ఇస్తాడు.

పాట పిలుపు–ప్రతిపిలుపు పద్ధతిలో సాగుతుంది; దాదాపు ప్రతి పాదాన్నీ పాడిన వెంటనే మళ్లీ వినిపిస్తారు, బహుశా కోరస్ బృందం. గాజులకు ‘గల్ గల్’, మట్టెలకు ‘జల్ జల్’ వంటి ధ్వని పదాలు లయను పెంచుతాయి. ఆమె చెంపల నడుమ మెరుపు మెరిస్తే తన గుండెల్లో వాన కురిసిందనే పోలిక పాటకు కవితాత్మకతను ఇస్తుంది. ‘మంజులా... నీ మేనబావను నే కాదా’ అనే పొడవైన పల్లవి ప్రతి చరణాన్నీ ముగిస్తుంది.
